s.def: The axis on a graph that is usually drawn left to right and usually shows the range of values of an independent variable.
Alternative letter-case form of X-ray.
ex: … analogous to x-ray image formation …

s.def: Alternative letter-case form of X-ray.

ety: From X + ray, a calque of German X-Strahl, coined by Wilhelm Röntgen upon his discovery of the rays in 1895, where X signifies their unknown nature. The chess sense is metaphorical, referring to control passing through a seemingly solid barrier.

s.def: A ray of short-wavelength electromagnetic radiation usually produced by bombarding a metal target in a vacuum. Used to create images of the internal structure of objects; this is possible because X-rays pass through most objects and can expose photographic film.
ex: X-rays are light with a wavelength between 0.1 and 10 nm.

s.def: A radiograph: an image made with X-rays.
ex: The doctor ordered some X-rays of my injured wrist.

s.def: An X-ray machine, a machine for performing radiography.
A tactical motif where a piece exerts influence or control over a square, piece, or line indirectly through another intervening piece.

ety: From Greek Ξάνθη (Xánthi).

s.def: A city in Thrace, northeastern Greece.
Alternative spelling of xanthine.

ety: From international scientific vocabulary, from French xanthine, reflecting New Latin combining forms: xanth- + -ine; ultimately from Ancient Greek ξανθός (xanthós, “yellow”), because xanthine is yellowish-white. By surface analysis, xanth- + -ine.

s.def: Any of a group of alkaloids that include caffeine, theophylline, and theobromine as well as the parent compound, a precursor of uric acid found in many organs of the body.

ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ξᾰνθός (xănthós, “yellow”).

s.def: yellow
derivative of xanthic acid

ety: From Xanthochroi.

s.def: Pertaining to the Xanthochroi; having fair hair and a pale complexion.
A member of the Xanthochroi.

ety: Etymology tree English xanth- Proto-Indo-European *-yéti Proto-Indo-European *-oyétider.? Ancient Greek -όω (-óō) Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ Proto-Hellenic *-mə Ancient Greek -μᾰ (-mă) Ancient Greek -ωμα (-ōma)der. English -oma English xanthoma From xanth- + -oma.

s.def: A small, yellow nodule, rich in cholesterol and other lipids, that occurs in the skin, often near a joint

ety: From xantho- + -phyll.

s.def: Any of various hydroxy, carbonyl or carboxylic acid derivatives of carotenes.
Lutein.

ety: By surface analysis, xanth- + -ous.

s.def: Yellow-brown; yolk-colored.
ex: Absorbent fatty xanthous histiocytes and xanthous granulations are observed in the marginal area of necrosis of the fatty tissue[…]

s.def: Pertaining to people with yellowish, red, auburn, or brown hair.
ex: The xanthous variety springs up out of every black-haired race.
[…] the xanthous, or fair class, comprises those who have brown, auburn, yellow, flaxen, or red hair; […]

ety: From French chebec, from Spanish xabeque or Catalan xabec or Italian sciabecco, from Arabic شُبَّاك (šubbāk, “fishing-net”). Not to confuse with the sambuq, an Indian-Sea vessel.

s.def: A small two-masted, and later three-masted, Mediterranean transport ship with an overhanging bow and stern.
ex: Winter. The green xebec whose figurehead was Astarte, goddess of sexual love, tacked slowly into the Grand Harbour.

ety: From Ancient Greek ξενία (xenía, “hospitality; relations of hospitality between states or between a person and a state; the status of an alien, i.e., not a citizen”), equivalent to xenia + -al.

s.def: Hospitable, especially to visiting strangers or foreigners.
Of the relation between a host and guest; friendly.

ety: Etymology tree Pre-Greekder. Proto-Hellenic *ksénwos Ancient Greek ξένϝος (xénwos) Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos)der. English xeno- Derived from Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos, “foreign, of a stranger”).

s.def: Having to do with foreigners.
ex: xenophilia, xenophobia

s.def: Relating to strangers or strangeness.
From a foreign place.
ex: xenolith, xenomenia

s.def: From a donor of another species.
ex: porcine xenograft

s.def: Of extraterrestrial origin.
ex: xeno- + archaeology → xenoarchaeology

ety: From xeno- + -genesis.

s.def: A foreign origin or source.
The production of an offspring that is unlike either of its parents.

ety: From xeno- + -glossia, borrowed from French xénoglossie.

s.def: Knowledge of a language one has never learned.
Glossolalia.

ety: From Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos, “foreign, strange”) + -on, used for all noble gases.

s.def: The chemical element (symbol Xe) with an atomic number of 54. It is a colorless, odorless, unreactive noble gas, used notably in camera flash technology.

ety: From Ancient Greek Ξενοφάνης (Xenophánēs). The name means “of foreign appearance” and is composed of ξένος (xénos, “foreign”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “appear”).

s.def: A Greek given name.
The pre-Socratic philosopher Xenophanes of Colophon; by extension or reference, any profound or transformative religious thinker.
ex: No Xenophanes arose amongst the Jews to rebuke them for ascribing to Jahweh acts which would be accounted a shame and a disgrace amongst men; […]
Euthyphro is no Xenophanes but as a religious and thinking man he can turn to great teachers; […]

ety: From xeno- + -phobe. From Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos, “foreign, strange”), + Ancient Greek φόβος (phóbos, “fear”).

s.def: One who hates or fears strangers or foreigners.
One who hates or fears extraterrestial life.

ety: From xeno- + -phobia.

s.def: A fear, antipathy, or hatred of strangers or foreigners.
ex: The United States is not the only country where xenophobia pays dividends for politicians.

s.def: A fear of aliens.

ety: From xeno- + -phobic, from Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos, “foreign, strange”) + φόβος (phóbos, “fear”).

s.def: Exhibiting or characterised by xenophobia, a fear or hatred of strangers, foreigners, or extraterrestial life.

ety: Etymology tree Pre-Greekder. Proto-Hellenic *ksénwos Ancient Greek ξένϝος (xénwos) Ancient Greek ξένος (xénos)der. English xeno- English transplantation English xenotransplantation From xeno- + transplantation.

s.def: The transplantation of biological or organic matter from a given species into a different one, especially when this matter has been altered (such as by genetic engineering)

ety: From Ancient Greek ξηρός (xērós, “dry”).

s.def: dry; dryness
Xerox; photocopying

ety: From xero- + -derma.

s.def: Any of various skin diseases characterised by dry, hard, scaly skin, especially ichthyosis.

ety: From xero- + -graphy.

s.def: A photocopying process in which a negative image formed on an electrically charged plate is transferred as a positive to paper and thermally fixed.

ety: From xero- + -philous.

s.def: Able to thrive in dry weather.
ex: The cactus is very xerophilous.

ety: From xero- + -osis.

s.def: Dryness.

ety: Genericized trademark from Xerox (“a photocopier”), from xerography, from Ancient Greek ξηρός (xērós, “dry”) and γραφή (graphḗ, “writing”).

s.def: A xerograph (copy).
ex: Near-synonyms: photocopy (broadly synonymous), photostat (broadly synonymous)
Hand me that xerox, would you?
There were twenty pictures in the envelope, xeroxes but clear enough. They documented the scene pretty much as I imagined it.

s.def: A xerographer (machine).
ex: Near-synonyms: photocopier, photoduplicator, copier (broadly synonymous), photostat (broadly synonymous)
The xerox broke down yesterday.

s.def: To make a copy using a xerographer.
ex: Near-synonyms: photocopy, photoduplicate (broadly synonymous), photostat (broadly synonymous)
I xeroxed the report for all the people at the meeting.

s.def: Initialism of Extensible Hypertext Markup Language, a reformulation of HTML as an XML application.

ety: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 習／习 (Xí).

s.def: Chinese surname
A surname from Chinese

ety: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of the Mandarin Chinese pronunciation for 新疆 (Xīnjiāng, “new territory, new frontier”), from 新 (xīn, “new”) + 疆 (jiāng, “territory, border, frontier”).

s.def: A Uyghur autonomous region of China, located in the sparsely populated northwest. Official name: Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. Capital: Ürümqi.
ex: Eighteen people remain trapped in a gold mine after it caved in China's northwestern province of Xinjiang.

ety: Borrowed from the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 匈奴 (Xiōngnú). Possibly a doublet of Hun; their relationship to the Huns is disputed.

s.def: An ancient nomadic-based people that formed a state or confederation north of the agriculture-based empire of the Han dynasty.

ety: Ancient Greek ξίφος (xíphos, “sword”) + English -i- (in place of the etymologically consistent -o-) + English sternum

s.def: Synonym of xiphoid process.

ety: From Ancient Greek ξιφοειδής (xiphoeidḗs, “sword-shaped”).

s.def: Shaped like a sword, ensiform.
Of or relating to the xiphoid process (also called xiphisternum).
The xiphoid process.
ex: In Asian pangolins the xiphoids are shorter[…]

s.def: Initialism of Extensible Markup Language, a flexible text format for creating structured computer documents in machine-readable form.
ex: 'XmL_3rr0R~/?$-HELP.i.am.trapped.in.the.newsbar!.^'

s.def: The logic function exclusive OR (as opposed to inclusive OR), whose output is true only when exactly one of its inputs is true.

ety: From German Xylem, from Ancient Greek ξύλον (xúlon, “wood”).

s.def: A vascular tissue in land plants primarily responsible for the distribution of water and minerals taken up by the roots; also the primary component of wood.

ety: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *kes-der. Proto-Indo-European *ksewlo-der.? Pre-Greekder.? Ancient Greek ξύλον (xúlon) English -itol English xylitol From Ancient Greek ξύλον (xúlon, “wood”) + English -itol (“anhydric alcohol”).

s.def: A pentahydric alcohol, C₅H₁₂O₅, penta-hydroxy pentane; derived from xylose; used as a sweetener.

ety: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *kes-der. Proto-Indo-European *ksewlo-der.? Pre-Greekder.? Ancient Greek ξῠ́λον (xŭ́lon) English xylo- From Ancient Greek ξῠ́λον (xŭ́lon, “wood”).

s.def: wood

ety: Back-formation from xylography, corresponding to xylo- (“wood”) + -graph.

s.def: An engraving in wood or woodcut, especially one used in printing predating the Western tradition (14th c.).
A print taken from such an engraving.
To make a print from an engraving in wood.

ety: From xylo- + -logy.

s.def: The study of wood.

ety: Etymology tree Ancient Greek ξῠ́λον (xŭ́lon) English xylo- Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂g- Proto-Indo-European *bʰh₂g-der. Ancient Greek ἔφαγον (éphagon) Ancient Greek -φάγος (-phágos)bor. Latin -phagusbor. English -phagous English xylophagous From xylo- (“wood”) + -phagous (“eating”).

s.def: Feeding on wood. (of insects etc.)
Destructive to wood. (of fungi etc.)

ety: From xylo- (“of wood”) + -phone (“sound”).

s.def: Any musical instrument (percussion idiophone) made of wooden slats graduated so as to make the sounds of the scale when struck with a small drumstick-like mallet; the standard Western concert xylophone or one of its derivatives.
ex: All I know how to play on my xylophone is "Mary Had a Little Lamb". Would you like to hear it?

ety: From Ancient Greek ξυστήρ (xustḗr, “scraper”), from ξύω (xúō, “scrape”).

s.def: A surgical instrument used to scrape bones.
